analysis:
Examined four changed files.

1. Darkbloom.swift head 171-228. registrationWeightHash returns a VerifiedWeightHashStore record, without re-reading the weights, for models with weightsVerifiedByManagedLoad. It does this when file identities match. Identities are captured before hashing, and the store is written only after a full computeHash. Registration weight hashes are already self-reported. Per T-012/T-027/SEC-007 and the WeightHasher.swift 63-68 comment, they guard only against accidental drift. A malicious operator (ADV-001) who edits the record file gains nothing beyond the existing ability to lie. No regression was identified.

Open contract (not supplied): the code comment claims the managed load SHA-256-verifies every file before serving. It also relies on VerifiedWeightHashStore.fileIdentities detecting in-place rewrites, e.g. via inode, size, mtime or ctime. T-041 binds SSD cache entries to the verified weightHash in coordinator mode. Integration should confirm that the reused hash cannot diverge from the bytes actually loaded, and which hash the SSD binding uses.

2. PageCache.swift (new, 1-61). It opens files O_RDONLY, checks fstat for S_IFREG, and makes a PROT_READ MAP_SHARED mapping. msync(MS_INVALIDATE) is best-effort; residentBytes uses mincore. It creates no new trust surface: it does not write file contents and adds no new path inputs. Paths come from the model snapshot, as before.

3. WeightHasher.swift head 250-253. The descriptor's page-cache drop runs in a defer before close, including on early-failure returns. The digest semantics and every fallback reader are unchanged.

4. StartupPreloader.swift. Adds an onFailure hook (default GLM5NextWiredLimitNotice.report) on load and self-test failures (lines 197, 221). This is an availability and diagnostic change only. Fail-open/fail-closed retirement is unchanged. Whether the notice prints sensitive error text to public logs is not visible here.

No findings qualify.
